provenance_detail: Synthesized from: 14.6B onboarding spec (step 4: entity type selection, step 5: business type selection, step 6-14: template-driven generation), 14.6B portfolio/entity/business ontology (entity taxonomy, business type catalog), 14.6B workflow/SOP engine spec (UBOS template library, 8 core workflows, template instantiation), 14.4 desired state canon (UBOS template library as franchise-like templates), 14.6B source detail preservation ledger (SIG-FEAT-019: template library, SIG-MOD-017: workflow templates). Operator has not specified individual template contents -- these are inferred from professional domain knowledge of each business type's standard operating needs.
description: UBOS (Universal Business Operating System) Template Library -- franchise-like starter templates for 18+ business types, defining default departments, workflows, roles, KPIs, agents, and industry-specific configurations that onboarding instantiates into a ready-to-operate business environment.
design_principles: Templates are franchise blueprints, not blank forms -- an operator selecting 'agency' gets a complete operating system for an agency, not a generic shell with labels changed
Every template encodes the accumulated operational wisdom of that business type -- the departments that actually exist, the workflows that actually run, the KPIs that actually matter
Templates are starting points, never cages -- operator customizes after generation, and EOS learns from those customizations to improve the template for future operators
Template quality is the single biggest determinant of first-boot experience quality -- a mediocre template means a mediocre first impression
Templates must be stage-aware -- a pre-revenue SaaS looks nothing like a scaling SaaS; the same template type adapts to the operator's declared stage
Templates carry provenance -- operators can see whether a template came from EOS defaults, community contribution, industry expert curation, or AI synthesis
Every template is testable -- you can spin up a template, inspect every generated artifact, and validate that the result is a coherent operating system before releasing it to production
Templates compose -- a holding company template instantiates sub-templates for each subsidiary type, creating nested operating systems that share governance

Deterministic spine: template selection, field population, and structure generation are deterministic. AI enhances descriptions, customizes tone, and suggests refinements within the generated structure

template_model.description: A BusinessTemplate is a versioned, composable blueprint that defines the default operational structure for a specific business type. When an operator selects a business type during onboarding (step 5), the corresponding template is instantiated, generating all departments, workflows, roles, KPIs, agents, and operational artifacts.

id.description: Unique identifier for the template definition

type_slug.description: Machine-readable business type identifier. Matches the business_type enum in the ontology.

name.description: Human-readable template name displayed in the onboarding type selector.

description.description: One-paragraph description of what this template creates. Shown in the onboarding type detail panel. Max 300 characters.

icon.description: Icon identifier from the EOS icon set for visual identification in the template picker.

industry_verticals.description: Industry verticals this template is designed for. Used for search/filter in the template library.

stage_adaptations.description: Stage-specific overrides. Keys are stage identifiers from the ontology (idea, validation, launch, early_revenue, growth, scale, maturity, exit). Each key contains partial overrides applied on top of the base template.

complexity_levels.description: Complexity-level overrides. Keys are solo_operator, small_team (2-5), growing_team (6-20), department_scale (20+). Each adjusts the number of departments, workflows, and agent configurations.

default_departments.description: Array of department definitions generated when this template is instantiated.

default_workflows.description: Array of workflow template references. Each points to a workflow definition in the UBOS workflow library with template-specific parameter overrides.

default_roles.description: Array of role definitions. Includes both human roles and AI agent roles.

default_kpis.description: Array of KPI definitions. Each includes the metric name, calculation method, target range, and reporting cadence.

default_agents.description: Array of AI agent configurations. Each maps to one of the 10 canonical EOS agents (CEO, Sales, Marketing, Finance, CS, HR, Legal, Ops, Product, Engineering) with template-specific instructions.

default_tasks.description: Array of seed tasks generated on first boot. Gives the operator immediate action items relevant to their business type and stage.

customization_points.description: Declared customization surfaces. Each identifies a field or section the operator is most likely to want to change, with guidance on how.

version.description: Semantic version of the template. Follows semver. Major = breaking structural change, minor = new fields/workflows added, patch = copy/config fixes.

provenance.description: Origin of this template. Determines trust level and curation status.

created_at.description: When this template version was created.

updated_at.description: When this template version was last modified.

usage_count.description: Number of times this template has been instantiated across all operators. Used for popularity ranking.

satisfaction_score.description: Aggregate satisfaction score from operators who used this template. 0.0-1.0 scale. Null if insufficient data.

versioning.description: Each template version is immutable once published. Updates create a new version. Existing instantiations are not affected by template updates -- operators can opt in to template upgrades via a 'sync with template' action that shows a diff of what would change.
versioning.migration_support: Template version upgrades generate a migration plan showing added/removed/changed departments, workflows, roles, and KPIs. Operator reviews and approves the migration before it executes.

customization.inheritance_model: Template provides defaults. Operator customizations override defaults. The link back to the template is preserved so the operator can see 'what changed from template' and 'what the template updated since you forked'.
customization.fork_behavior: When an operator customizes beyond a threshold (>40% of fields changed), the system suggests 'forking' the template -- creating a new template from their customized version that can be shared back to the community.
customization.constraint_propagation: Customizing a department name propagates to all workflows, roles, and KPIs that reference that department. Deleting a department triggers a review of orphaned workflows.

default_agents.template_instructions: Strategic oversight for a service business. Focus on client portfolio health, team utilization balance, and revenue diversification. Flag client concentration risk when any single client exceeds 30% of revenue.
Agency sales cycle: qualify on budget + timeline + fit. Generate proposals from project scope templates. Track pipeline velocity and flag stalled deals at 14 days.
Agency marketing = thought leadership + case studies + referral cultivation. Prioritize case study production from completed projects. Track inbound lead source attribution.
Project-based financial tracking. Calculate margin per project and per client. Flag projects trending below 30% margin. Chase overdue invoices at 7, 14, and 30 days.

Client success in agency context = proactive health monitoring. Track deliverable satisfaction, response times, and scope creep indicators. Trigger upsell workflow when client signals expansion needs.
Resource allocation across concurrent projects. Maintain utilization between 70-85% (below = underutilized, above = burnout risk). Flag capacity conflicts 2 weeks ahead.

default_agents.template_instructions: SaaS strategic oversight. Monitor MRR trajectory, burn rate, and runway. Flag when growth rate declines two consecutive months. Track competitive moves. Prepare board-ready metrics.
Feature prioritization using RICE scoring. Track feature requests by customer segment. Monitor activation metrics. Flag features with low adoption post-launch.
Technical health monitoring. Track deployment frequency, failure rate, and recovery time. Flag tech debt accumulation. Enforce code review and testing standards.
SaaS sales cycle: demo-driven with trial conversion. Track pipeline by stage and conversion rates between stages. Flag deals stalled >7 days. Calculate and report win/loss reasons.
Demand generation focus. Track CAC by channel. Monitor content performance by traffic and conversion. Manage SEO keyword rankings. Report on marketing-sourced pipeline weekly.
Health-score-driven customer management. Calculate health from product usage, support tickets, and engagement signals. Proactive outreach when health drops. Track expansion revenue opportunities.
SaaS financial modeling. Track MRR waterfall (new, expansion, contraction, churn). Calculate unit economics monthly. Monitor cash burn and update runway projections. Revenue recognition per ASC 606.

composition_behavior.description: The holding company template is unique in that it composes sub-templates. When a holding company is created, each subsidiary entity within it triggers its own business type template instantiation. The holding company layer provides governance, reporting, and shared services on top of the individual business operating systems.
composition_behavior.sub_template_instantiation: Each subsidiary gets its own full EOS environment with the template matching its business type. The holding company provides a consolidated view across all subsidiaries.

sources.description: Templates shipped with EOS. Professionally designed based on industry best practices. Reviewed by domain experts before inclusion. The 18 templates in this artifact are eos_default templates.
sources.quality_bar: Must have all required fields populated, at least 5 workflows, 5 KPIs, 4 roles, and 3 agent configurations. Must be tested through the spinup engine with zero errors.

sources.description: Templates generated by AI from operator descriptions of their business. When an operator selects 'other' during onboarding, the system synthesizes a custom template from their description, industry, and stage. The synthesized template uses the closest default template as a base and adapts.
sources.quality_bar: Must pass structural validation (all required fields). Flagged as ai_synthesized so operators know it has not been human-reviewed.

sources.description: Templates shared by operators who forked and improved default templates. Must pass quality review before appearing in the public library.
sources.quality_bar: Structural validation + community rating > 4.0 + at least 3 successful instantiations by other operators.

sources.description: Templates created or reviewed by verified industry professionals. Highest trust tier. Potential revenue stream via premium template marketplace.
sources.quality_bar: Structural validation + expert identity verification + editorial review by EOS team.

sources.description: Private templates created when an operator customizes beyond 40% divergence from the base template. Not shared publicly unless the operator opts in.
sources.quality_bar: Structural validation only. Private to the operator's account.

customization_workflow: Generated operating system is immediately functional with all defaults
Operator can customize any element: rename departments, add/remove workflows, adjust KPIs, modify agent instructions
System tracks divergence from base template as a percentage
At 40% divergence, system suggests forking into a new template
Forked templates retain link to parent for future template update comparison
customization_constraints: Operator cannot remove the last department or the last workflow
Operator cannot remove the CEO agent (core governance requirement)
KPI calculations must be syntactically valid (system validates formulas)
Role authority scopes must not create orphaned escalation chains
All customizations are reversible -- operator can reset any element to template default

evolution.template_update_cycle: EOS team reviews and updates default templates quarterly based on: operator customization patterns (what do operators change most?), community feedback, industry changes, and internal quality audits.
evolution.backward_compatibility: Template updates never break existing instantiations. Updates create a new version. Operators on previous versions are notified and can preview changes before opting in.
evolution.learning_from_operators: The system aggregates anonymized customization patterns to identify: frequently added departments, frequently removed workflows, commonly adjusted KPIs. These patterns inform the next template version.
evolution.deprecation: Templates can be deprecated but never deleted. Deprecated templates remain functional for existing users but are removed from the template picker for new instantiations.

community_contribution.submission_process: Operator opts to share their forked template -> structural validation -> community review period (30 days) -> quality threshold check -> publish to community library
community_contribution.incentive_model: Contributors earn platform credit for templates that achieve high adoption. Top contributors earn 'Template Author' badge and potential revenue share on premium templates.
community_contribution.moderation: Community templates are flagged for review if they receive negative ratings or contain inappropriate content. EOS team has final authority on community library contents.

spinup_engine.description: The Spinup Engine is the runtime process that transforms a template selection into a fully configured business operating environment. It runs during onboarding (steps 5-14) and can be re-run when adding new entities to an existing portfolio.
trigger_points: Onboarding step 5: operator selects business type
Portfolio management: operator adds new entity
Template upgrade: operator opts into new template version

spinup_steps.name: template_selection
spinup_steps.description: Operator selects a business type from the template picker. System loads the corresponding template definition.

spinup_steps.name: stage_adaptation
spinup_steps.description: System applies stage-specific overrides based on the operator's declared business stage (from onboarding step 7 or entity configuration). This adjusts departments, workflows, and focus areas.

spinup_steps.name: complexity_adaptation
spinup_steps.description: System applies complexity-level overrides based on team size / operator configuration (from onboarding step 8). This adjusts the number and depth of departments, workflows, and agents.

spinup_steps.name: department_generation
spinup_steps.description: System creates department records from the adapted template. Each department gets a name, slug, purpose description, and initial configuration. Departments are entity-scoped.

spinup_steps.name: role_generation
spinup_steps.description: System creates role records for each department. Roles include permission sets, responsibilities, and escalation chains. For solo operators, all roles are initially assigned to the operator.

spinup_steps.name: workflow_instantiation
spinup_steps.description: System creates workflow instances from the template's workflow definitions. Each workflow gets concrete steps, triggers, and ownership assignments based on the generated roles. Workflow definitions are pulled from the UBOS workflow library and parameterized for this entity.

spinup_steps.name: kpi_instantiation
spinup_steps.description: System creates KPI tracking records from the template's KPI definitions. Each KPI gets a target range (based on stage), a reporting cadence, and a responsible department/role. Initial targets are AI-suggested based on industry benchmarks and operator's declared stage.

spinup_steps.name: agent_configuration
spinup_steps.description: System configures AI agents from the template's agent definitions. Each agent gets the canonical agent's base soul document plus template-specific instructions. Agent capabilities are scoped to the entity's departments and workflows. Agent authority levels are set based on operator's trust preference (from onboarding).

spinup_steps.name: task_seeding
spinup_steps.description: System generates initial tasks from the template's task definitions plus stage-appropriate startup tasks. These give the operator immediate action items upon entering active mode. Tasks are assigned to the operator (solo) or appropriate roles (team).

spinup_steps.name: validation_and_activation
spinup_steps.description: System runs a structural validation pass: all departments have at least one role, all workflows have valid owner assignments, all KPIs have valid calculation formulas, all agents have valid scope. If validation passes, the entity is marked as active and the operator enters the workspace.

defaults_applied.naming: Template names are applied as-is. Operator can rename anything post-spinup.
defaults_applied.ordering: Departments are ordered as defined in the template. Operator can reorder in the UI.
defaults_applied.visibility: All generated elements are visible by default. Operator can hide/archive elements they do not need yet.
defaults_applied.ai_trust_level: Default is 'supervised' -- agents can draft but not execute without operator approval. Operator can upgrade to 'autonomous' per-agent post-spinup.

customization_points.description: Operator can preview the template before spinup and toggle departments/workflows on or off. This is shown in onboarding step 6 (entity configuration).
customization_points.user_action: Toggle checkboxes next to departments and workflows

customization_points.description: The spinup process is visible in real-time (not a loading screen). Operator sees each element being created and can pause to rename or adjust before continuing.
customization_points.user_action: Click any generated element to rename or edit inline

customization_points.description: Full customization available in the workspace. Operator can add/remove/modify any generated element. Changes are tracked as divergence from the template.

error_handling.template_not_found: Fall back to a generic 'custom business' template that has minimal structure (3 departments, 3 workflows, 5 KPIs) and prompts the operator for more information.
error_handling.validation_failure: Spinup rolls back all generated records and presents the operator with specific errors and remediation suggestions.
error_handling.partial_generation: If spinup fails partway through (e.g., agent configuration fails), the successfully generated elements are preserved and the failed step is retried with degraded defaults.

open_questions.question: Should the template library be curated-only (EOS team controls all templates) or community-driven (operators can share templates publicly)?
open_questions.recommendation: hybrid_curated_plus_community -- EOS defaults are curated; community section has separate quality bar and trust signals
open_questions.impact: Determines whether to build community contribution infrastructure and moderation tools

open_questions.question: Should premium templates (industry expert created) be a monetization vector? If so, what revenue share model?
open_questions.recommendation: subscription_tier_gated -- premium templates included in higher subscription tiers, not individually priced, to avoid marketplace friction
open_questions.impact: Affects subscription tier design, template author incentive model, and marketplace infrastructure

open_questions.question: Should the template marketplace be internal to EOS or a public-facing storefront that drives awareness and user acquisition?
open_questions.recommendation: public_browse_private_use -- anyone can browse and preview templates (marketing/SEO value), but instantiation requires an EOS account
open_questions.impact: Affects SEO strategy, public API design, and marketing funnel

open_questions.question: How many business types should ship in V1 vs be added incrementally?
open_questions.recommendation: top_8_at_launch (agency, saas, ecommerce, consulting, freelance, education, media_company, marketplace) plus 'custom/other' with AI synthesis. Remaining 10 added in V1.1-V1.3 based on demand signals.
open_questions.impact: Affects launch timeline, QA burden, and template quality assurance

open_questions.question: Should template instantiation be fully deterministic or should AI personalize the generated output based on operator's business description?
open_questions.recommendation: deterministic_with_ai_enhancement -- structural generation is deterministic (departments, workflows, KPIs always the same for a given template+stage+complexity), AI enhances descriptions, task priorities, and KPI targets based on operator context
open_questions.impact: Affects consistency, testability, and the degree to which two operators with the same selections get identical environments

implementation_notes.data_model: Templates are stored as JSON documents in the database with a relational index for type_slug, version, provenance, and industry_verticals. Template instantiation creates normalized relational records (departments, workflows, roles, KPIs, agents) linked back to the source template and version.
implementation_notes.template_schema_versioning: The template schema itself (the shape of a BusinessTemplate object) follows semver independently of individual template versions. Schema v2 might add new fields that all templates must support.
implementation_notes.integration_with_onboarding: The template library is the engine behind onboarding steps 5-14. The onboarding spec (phase14_6b_eos_onboarding_first_boot_spec.json) defines the user-facing flow; this artifact defines the template data and spinup logic behind it.
implementation_notes.integration_with_workflow_engine: Template workflow definitions reference the UBOS workflow library defined in phase14_6b_eos_workflow_sop_engine_spec.json. The spinup engine resolves workflow template references into concrete workflow instances using the workflow engine's instantiation API.
implementation_notes.integration_with_agent_architecture: Template agent configurations reference the 10 canonical EOS agents defined in phase14_6b_eos_agent_architecture_spec.json. The spinup engine creates entity-scoped agent instances with template-specific instruction overlays.
implementation_notes.integration_with_ontology: Business types, stages, and complexity levels align with the taxonomy defined in phase14_6b_eos_portfolio_entity_business_ontology.json. The template type_slug matches the business type enum in the ontology.
